Up close: A buffalo-check plaid of forest green and near-black squares, about 12px each, with a fine diagonal twill thread texture inside, crossed by thin cream windowpane lines about 45px apart, with a few stray white lint flecks. Clear and well-contrasted, not faint. From a distance: Reads as a dark green and black plaid; the cream grid is the first thing to survive at distance as a fine lattice, and the colour mix looks like a dark forest checkerboard. Measured spec (average): metal 2, roughness 206, coat 224. Shine: matte. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Flannel: Flannel Forest" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: plaid reads on every panel; keeps the flannel feel
Hood and doors: large flat areas show the check size
Large white or cream numbers with a thick black outline read; green and black numbers are lost in the squares.
Plain black or cream blocks: calm areas next to the check
Pairs well with: cream, tan leather, matte black, chrome.
pitfalls: Not red buffalo check: it is forest green and black with cream windowpane lines
Not carbon fibre or weave: squares are large and printed, not woven fibre
Avoid: dark numbers on dark plaid, large flat black areas.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 2 (non-metal paint), roughness 206 (flat), clearcoat 224 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers on dark plaid, large flat black areas.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: plain black or cream blocks: calm areas next to the check; chrome or white pinstripes: crisp lines against the matte plaid
Patterns to avoid: other plaid, check or grid patterns: duplicate and moire; glitter or holo: wrong mood
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear patches: shiny panels against the matte flannel; matte stripe spec: not needed, already matte
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Cdrom: Floppy Black
articles.summary: Anthracite matte plastic with scattered brushed-metal shutter slivers laid in a loose brick pattern; dark, low-saturation, subtle sparkle. Reads as a dark industrial sci-fi panel; the slivers show as scattered silver dashes on near-black, the rest is a busy, low-contrast charcoal.
articles.what: Anthracite matte magnetic-disk casing material, fragmented shutter-like brushed slivers. Up close: Dark charcoal plate packed with rectangular recessed slots, ribbed vent panels, small square holes and a few bright brushed-steel slivers, all in horizontal and vertical blocks, with tiny chipped light flecks at some corners. Slivers are 20-60 px wide. From a distance: Reads as a dark industrial sci-fi panel; the slivers show as scattered silver dashes on near-black, the rest is a busy, low-contrast charcoal. Measured spec (average): metal 19, roughness 92, coat 94. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Cdrom: Floppy Black" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: large flat panels show the block layout
Avoid small trim: the blocks turn to noise
Dark numbers vanish; use white, red or orange numbers with an outline because the blocks are busy.
Fine grain or noise: small extra grit that does not fight the blocks
Pairs well with: silver, red, white, orange.
pitfalls: Not plain matte black: the block layout is clearly visible and busy
Not carbon fibre: no weave, the shapes are rectangles and vents
Avoid: dark areas swallow numbers, next to other dark finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 19 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 92 (satin gloss), clearcoat 94 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark areas swallow numbers, next to other dark finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine grain or noise: small extra grit that does not fight the blocks; thin carbon weave at low strength: same techy mood, still readable
Patterns to avoid: camo: blotches over blocks look like a mess; bold stripes or text-like patterns: the blocks already read as text noise
Spec overlays that work: fine sparkle: adds glints on the steel slivers; roughness variation: makes recessed slots look deeper
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Fresh: Fresh Kicks
articles.summary: Pale white satin surface with soft curved mesh and leather patches, bright and near-colourless. Reads as a clean off-white with a soft quilted, bubbly texture; no colour, a light grey cast in the shadows of the seams.
articles.what: White patent leather and bright shoe mesh abstracted as small curved mixed-material patches. Up close: All-white sneaker material cut into curved patches 30-60 px wide with stitched seams: puffy glossy patent-leather pads, perforated mesh with rows of small holes, and fine ribbed panels. Only whites and pale greys, with relief shading making the shapes read. From a distance: Reads as a clean off-white with a soft quilted, bubbly texture; no colour, a light grey cast in the shadows of the seams. Measured spec (average): metal 12, roughness 78, coat 85. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
